newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE urged to ban expats from wearing local robes.
newsitem.headline: UAE urged to ban expats from wearing local robes.

text.p: Citizens of the United Arab Emirates are urging the state to ban foreigners from wearing the country's national costume, saying "misuse" of the flowing white gowns and headscarves could bring disrepute to Gulf Arabs.

The Gulf News daily said on Wednesday that UAE nationals were increasingly worried about foreigners donning men's traditional dress, known as "kandoora". The national symbol should only be worn by nationals, they say.
"We are no longer able to tell our own people from kandoora-clad expatriates," said a woman named Aisha.
"Any misbehaviour they commit will be at the nationals' expense because in their attire they will be mistaken for nationals," the paper quoted her as saying.
Foreigners, mostly from the Indian subcontinent but also from the Philippines and other south-east Asian countries, account for about 75 percent of the UAE's 2.4 million people.
To try to reduce the vast number of expatriates working in the oil-rich Gulf state, the UAE has announced tough new immigration laws from October.
Expatriates interviewed by the Gulf News said they preferred wearing the kandoora because it was cheap, comfortable in the sweltering heat, and earned instant respect from nationals.
"I have discovered that by wearing a kandoora I get better treatment wherever I go, because people think I am a "muwaten", a national," said a Bangladeshi quoted by the paper.
